# MCP tools and profiles

This page is the tool catalogue of the Odoo MCP server this release ships, version 1.1.0 at commit [`9f5c5afa6785`](https://github.com/unstaticlabs/odoo-mcp/commit/9f5c5afa6785b2244bf16a50909d13040ef72d3b), copied from its own documentation. Links to the server's other documents open that same commit on GitHub. Bump the pin in `deploy/odoo-mcp/release.json`, then run `make docs-mcp` to regenerate it; edits to the page itself are overwritten.

The executable source of truth is the canonical registry created in `src/capabilities/index.ts`. This document describes selection policy; tool schemas and module predicates come from code.

This document is also the single owner of the surface numbers. Other documents
refer here instead of repeating them.

## Current default surface

| Measure | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Tools on `/mcp` with every feature available | 36 |
| Tools on `/mcp` without document materialization | 34 |
| Estimated input/output schema tokens on `/mcp` | 20,940 |
| Budget enforced by `/readyz` (`DEFAULT_PROFILE_SCHEMA_TOKEN_BUDGET`) | 21,000 |

Odoo module, method, and access availability can lower the counts further.
Schema estimates are not measured model usage. Update this table, and only this
table, when the surface changes.

## MCP risk annotations

Each public tool explicitly advertises `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, and `openWorldHint`. Bounded Odoo reads and specialized draft/preparatory actions stay in the authenticated private workspace and have `openWorldHint=false`. Generic arbitrary-model writes and public-method dispatch remain conservatively classified because Odoo business hooks may overwrite data or contact third parties.

`odoo_add_internal_note` appends an internal-subtype note with zero direct recipients and `notify_skip_followers=true`. This skips native Chatter follower and direct-recipient notifications; ordinary model hooks still run. It is not idempotent. `odoo_post_message` remains available for notifying comments and other Chatter workflows. A comment (`mail.mt_comment`) is posted with `message_type=comment`, so Odoo draws it as the message a person sends; a note keeps Odoo's default type.

Annotations describe behavior, not a bypass for host safety checks or server authorization. Inspect emitted `tools/list` and compare real scheduled-run results before claiming any safety regression fixed.

## Discovery and read primitives

The preferred discovery and read tools are:

| Tool | Selection rule |
| --- | --- |
| `odoo_search_capabilities` | Find semantic helpers or actions by intent across several toolsets. Not on `/mcp`; see below. |
| `docs_search` | Find ranked user-guide pages, descriptions, matching text and canonical links. Native internal-user guide access applies. |
| `odoo_search_models` | Find accessible technical models from authenticated API metadata. |
| `odoo_describe_model` | Inspect fields and public method signatures before guessing. |
| `odoo_search_records` | Search across models and read nested relations in one call. |
| `odoo_read_records` | Read known record IDs, flat or with a nested `specification`. |

`odoo_search_capabilities` is deliberately absent from `/mcp`. That profile lists
its whole surface statically, so catalogue search there only spends caller context
to describe tools the caller can already see. It remains on `/mcp/all`, where
deferred loading hides most schemas, and on the thematic and `/mcp/read-only`
profiles, which each expose a subset of the catalogue and where
`visible_in_current_profile` and the recommended fallback still carry information.

Further generic substrate tools are available in every writable profile:

- `odoo_aggregate_records` and `odoo_describe_environment`;
- `odoo_create_records`, `odoo_update_records`, `odoo_archive_records`, `odoo_post_message`, and `odoo_call_method`.

`odoo_submit_feedback` is also present in every writable MCP profile. It lets any active governed Agent create one structured, low-trust report in the configured MCP development Inbox, even when that Agent has no Project application access. The Odoo method fixes and validates the destination, escapes all submitted text, and creates the task plus its audit marker in one transaction. The explicit `/mcp/read-only` transport profile hides it because that profile contains no mutations.

The only advanced-only generic tool is `odoo_delete_records`.

Use `odoo_call_method` when a legitimate public Distribution method has no MCP shortcut or when preserving a model's versatile public API is more useful than adding a thin wrapper. Prefer a fixed-intent action when it reduces ambiguity, returns better context, or guarantees a multi-step invariant. A method Odoo publishes as `readonly` runs under the read contract and is retried like any other read; every other method receives one attempt and may report unknown completion. The returned `execution.mode` states which contract applied.

## Semantic catalogue

Use `docs_search` for guidance before inventing a workflow. It reads the running release’s guide through `usl.docs.guide.search_pages`; generic `odoo_call_method` access remains available for full page steps and screenshot references via `read_page`. Use `fr` or `en` to filter by language. Regional locales such as `fr_FR` and `en-US` find the same guides. Omit the language to search all translations. Abstract guide access is authorized by Odoo, without requiring CRUD metadata.

Current context helpers cover partners, record activities, project tasks, invoices, individual expenses, expense batches, Home attention, B2C orders, the rebuilt Accounting overview/reports, and the USL document archive. They return bounded high-signal context and warnings when optional linked context cannot be read.

The connector and Odoo are released independently. When a context helper's own field list names a field this Odoo release does not have yet, the helper reads again once without it, asks native `fields_get` once, and returns a warning naming the model and field in `warnings`; the record simply lacks that field. Any other error, and every field a caller names in a generic tool (`odoo_read_records`, `odoo_search_records`, `odoo_aggregate_records`, `odoo_call_method`), reaches the caller unchanged.

The Accounting overview keeps all-date ledger totals separate from the open annual
closing workspace and latest operational closing. Its legacy `draft_expense_count`
means expenses still to process: draft, submitted and approved. It is not an
editable-draft count. New servers also return `draft_only_expense_count`,
`submitted_expense_count` and `approved_expense_count` from that same company
view. `_scope` states these meanings and whether the additive fields are available.
Older servers remain readable; missing breakdowns are omitted with a warning,
never replaced with zero. The shortcut negotiates only these optional fields
through native `fields_get`, then reads one overview snapshot. It does not require
additional expense-row access or grant permission to edit any expense.

The invoice helper optionally accepts `company_change: {target_company_id, offset, limit}` for one native read-only snapshot of company choices, all line types, actual financial links, origins and evidence. Each page is an independent snapshot with readable-scope counts and explicit truncation or unavailability. Default invoice context remains unchanged. This option adds no company-change action or approval. To move a draft vendor bill, use `accounting_change_bill_company`.

Document tools use the Distribution archive facade for search, context, bounded text, similarity, and catalogues. Link/unlink operations call one public archive method. `documents_create_download_url` is a consequential action that issues a 30–900 second HTTPS bearer URL for one exact authorized document version; `documents_revoke_download_url` ends that capability early. Both are static on `/mcp` when available and deferred only on `/mcp/all`. Search and read tools report binary availability but never create or return bearer URLs. For supported files up to 4 MiB, `documents_get_content` with an explicit `binary` selection instead returns verified bytes through the existing authenticated connector: common images as MCP image content, other files as embedded resources. The host decides how to open an embedded PDF; receipt of bytes alone is not a claim of model vision. Older servers retain ordinary text reads; a binary request explains when its native method is unavailable. Issuance does not prove the client downloaded bytes; see the [qualification runbook](https://github.com/unstaticlabs/odoo-mcp/blob/9f5c5afa6785b2244bf16a50909d13040ef72d3b/docs/document-materialization.md).

Thin domain list/get wrappers are intentionally absent where generic search/read already communicates the task cleanly.

### Task, project and contact content relevance

On a Distribution release supporting native relevance order, use
`odoo_search_records` on `project.task`, `project.project` or `res.partner`:
pass `domain: [["usl_search_text", "ilike", query]]`,
`order: "usl_search_text"`, and `context: {search_relevance_query: query}`.
Choose the same `company_ids`, `lang` and `active_test: false` as Home.
At the same identity and scope, each model has Home's title-first order and
descending-ID tie breaker. Existing domains can add ordinary filters.
Use `fields` for a flat selection or `specification` for related fields.
Delegated read-only profiles can use either once the Distribution classifies
the model’s native `web_search_read` as read-only. If an older release returns
`agent_read_only_action_denied` for that method, use `fields` to continue
within the same company and record permissions.
This non-ID order uses offset cursors; unchanged records and access give stable
pages, but edits between requests can change the result set.

Discover `usl_search_text` through `odoo_describe_model`; its help advertises this
conditional order on supported releases. Without the explicit query context,
the virtual field still reports itself as not ordinarily sortable. Older releases reject this order: do not silently
substitute an ID order while claiming relevance. Omit it or select another
native `order` for ordinary generic search. Those paths retain their existing
order and pagination.

Task message evidence additionally uses `context.search_source_query` and the
readable `usl_search_sources` field. Record and source rights remain native and
are rechecked on each read. This path does not call or grant access to the
abstract Home service, and does not perform fuzzy retrieval.

## Card maintenance

`projects_update_task` writes stage, state, description, link (`github_url`) and Sources references of one task in a single `web_save`; state is required with a stage because Odoo resets it otherwise. `activities_complete` marks activities done through `action_feedback`. Both are static on `/mcp`; see [keeping a project card](https://github.com/unstaticlabs/odoo-mcp/blob/9f5c5afa6785b2244bf16a50909d13040ef72d3b/docs/projects-cards.md) for what belongs where.

## Everyday workflows on `/mcp`

These workflows are complete on the default profile without a profile switch:

| Workflow | Static tools on `/mcp` |
| --- | --- |
| Find and read documents | `documents_search`, `documents_get_context`, `documents_get_content` |
| Obtain original bytes and clean up | `documents_create_download_url`, `documents_revoke_download_url` |
| Create and maintain tasks | `projects_create_task`, `projects_get_task_context`, `projects_update_task`, `odoo_update_records` |
| Chatter and follow-ups | `odoo_add_internal_note` (no notifications), `odoo_post_message` (may notify), `activities_list_for_record`, `activities_schedule`, `activities_complete` |
| Prepare expenses | `expenses_get_context`, `expenses_update_draft` |
| Split a draft or correct all linked parts | `expenses_split_draft`, `expenses_correct_draft_family` |
| Prepare vendor bills/credit notes | `accounting_get_invoice_context`, `expenses_configure_draft_vendor_bill` |
| Report a connector issue | `odoo_submit_feedback` |

`expenses_update_draft` uses one native transaction and returns the final expense.
Servers supporting financial snapshots also return optional `financial_comparison`
with native `before` and `after` read records from that transaction. The MCP passes
these through without calculating taxes or deltas. Amounts ending in `_currency`
use `currency_id` (document currency); `total_amount`, `untaxed_amount`, and
`tax_amount` use `company_currency_id`, including `untaxed_amount` despite its
upstream field metadata. Older servers can omit the comparison.
For a draft company correction, supply a matching employee and select both
authorized companies in `context.allowed_company_ids`. Replace incompatible
category/account links or clear them with `false`; clear taxes with `[]` and
analytics with `{}`. A batch or supplier bill/vendor from the previous company
also needs an explicit compatible replacement or clear. Odoo preserves receipt
identity and document currency, recalculates the target company amount, and
records the company correction in Chatter. Submitted or accounted expenses are
refused. Split ownership requires a coordinated family correction; this shortcut
does not silently move sibling expenses. The generic ORM tools remain available
under their normal native access rules.

Task context includes dependency enablement, readable open blockers with canonical
links, and a reason for Waiting. Dependency details are capped at 100 and read
under the caller's own rights. Completeness uses the native task UI's aggregate
dependency count, because relational reads can already hide inaccessible IDs.
Only readable blocker records are linked; raw relation IDs are not returned.
`complete: false` means missing details must not
be treated as proof that no blocker exists. Manual or stale Waiting and disabled
dependencies are distinguished from a proven dependency-derived wait. This
read-only view does not change task state or repair historical tasks.

A task can also wait for something outside Odoo. Its reason is the ordinary field
`usl_waiting_reason` (with an optional contact, `usl_waiting_partner_id`). Task
context returns both, and `waiting_reason` is `external_reason` while one is set;
read and write them with the generic record tools. Setting a reason makes the task
Waiting; clearing it, or writing state In Progress, resumes it. To wait for another
task, use native dependencies.

For different accounting components, `expenses_split_draft` accepts explicit
gross lines and delegates to the native split wizard. Their sum must match the
source at its currency precision. Signed discounts and zero components retain
native behavior; no percentage tax is invented for a direct import-VAT account.
The source becomes the first part and stays the native origin. Every result
includes a direct record URL and the before/after document totals, with copied
source evidence and its checksum preserved.

`expenses_get_context` exposes the split origin and count. Review the whole
visible family before calling `expenses_correct_draft_family`: name every part,
the common target company/employee, and one explicit mapping choice per part.
Compatible defaults remain; incompatible financial or Batch links require named
replacements or clears. A hidden or non-draft part, changed membership or invalid
mapping leaves all parts unchanged. The reply reports document totals grouped by
currency rather than summing different currencies together. Both shortcuts use
one native transaction and never submit, post, pay or reconcile. Unknown
completion always requires readback before another action.

`accounting_change_bill_company` moves one draft vendor bill or credit note to another company the caller can access, in two calls. The first call (no `confirm`) writes nothing and returns the native `account.move.change_bill_company` preview: blockers with links and next steps, the proposed journal, fiscal position, payment terms and payable account, each line from and to with accounts and taxes, unresolved items, and the destination tax totals and due dates, with a `preview_id`. The second call passes `confirm: true` and that `preview_id` (and the same `mapping`, if any) and applies it in one Odoo transaction, returning the bill before and after. Each call is one transport attempt. After a lost reply, read the bill: a bill already in the destination reports `already_done` when confirmed again. It is listed in the `accounting` profile and on `/mcp/all`, not on `/mcp`, to keep the default surface within its schema budget. It requires the Distribution release that publishes `change_bill_company`.

Activity rescheduling and editing use the generic update tool where Odoo
permits it; completion uses the documented public method via `odoo_call_method`.
Less common document linking and catalogue operations, and expense approval and
posting, live in the thematic profiles or behind the inspected public-method
fallback rather than on `/mcp`.

Prefer a matching visible workflow tool. On `/mcp` every tool is listed, so there
is nothing further to discover there. Keep `/mcp/all` for clients with verified
host-side tool search. Reconnect and start a new ChatGPT conversation before
comparing the actual tool list and running the golden prompts.

## Business action catalogue

Current actions cover:

- project task creation and small task attachments;
- cross-domain activity scheduling;
- draft expense/vendor-bill preparation and individual expense transitions;
- expense-batch context application and submit/approve/post transitions;
- document link/unlink;
- explicit short-lived document materialization and revocation;
- draft incoming vendor-receipt creation with a no-call dry run.
- structured Agent feedback submission to the governed MCP development Inbox.

Actions do not bypass Odoo state or permissions. The agent should read the relevant context immediately before consequential operations. Mutation failures are not automatically replayed.

## Profiles

| URL | Intended visible surface |
| --- | --- |
| `/mcp` | Static everyday workflows plus generic substrate; the measured schema budget is shown above. |
| `/mcp/all` | Complete catalogue with deferred-loading metadata. |
| `/mcp/read-only` | Every read capability currently available. |
| `/mcp/accounting` | Universal core plus accounting, expenses, and related document actions. |
| `/mcp/projects` | Universal core plus project and related capabilities. |
| `/mcp/documents` | Universal core plus archive and related capabilities. |
| `/mcp/b2c` | Universal core plus B2C context. |
| `/mcp/advanced` | Default plus permanent deletion. |

Clients should use `/mcp` or a fitting profile. These named profiles omit `_meta.defer_loading` so hosted clients receive every listed schema as a static callable surface. `/mcp/all` is available only when a client deliberately wants the complete catalogue and emits per-tool deferred-loading hints. Those hints do not make a schema callable unless the client actually loads that tool definition.

### Progressive-discovery client compatibility

Progressive discovery is a host capability, not an MCP server-side profile switch. Use `/mcp/all` only with a host that searches and materializes MCP tool definitions itself:

- OpenAI Responses API agents support tool search with GPT-5.4 and later when the request includes `tool_search` and marks the hosted MCP server `defer_loading: true`. OpenAI documents deferral on the Responses API MCP-server tool definition, not automatic interpretation of arbitrary per-tool MCP result metadata.
- Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK enable MCP tool search by default with Sonnet 4+ and Opus 4+; Haiku does not support it. Their host defers and materializes registered MCP tools.
- GitHub Copilot CLI enables on-demand tool loading on supported Claude and GPT-5.4+ models when its tool-count threshold is reached. Its `deferTools` setting is host configuration.

Hosted ChatGPT plugin connections are not documented as providing that host-controlled materialization flow, and production testing currently shows catalogue discovery without callable-schema materialization. Keep those connections on the static `/mcp` endpoint.

References: [OpenAI tool search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search), [Claude Code MCP tool search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#scale-with-mcp-tool-search), and [GitHub Copilot CLI tool search](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/tool-search).

Module, public-method, model-access, and feature predicates remove specialized tools from `tools/list` unless positive availability is known. Capability search evaluates the complete canonical catalogue: it omits entries proven unavailable, retains unknown candidates, and returns `availability`, `visible_in_current_profile`, and `callable_now`. On writable profiles its optional fallback prefers a matching callable tool, then `odoo_call_method`; on `read-only` it always recommends generic record search and never method invocation. Search metadata is advisory and never activates a tool, changes a profile, or alters `tools/list`.

## Contract conventions

- Tool names are stable snake_case actions; capability IDs are stable dotted identifiers.
- Schemas are strict and bounded. Unknown input keys fail validation.
- Results use structured MCP output plus concise text compatibility.
- Record references use `{model,id,display_name,url}` and the public Odoo origin.
- Read/write/consequential/irreversible effects and MCP annotations describe behavior; they do not authorize it.
- Search and read calls select fields and bound result counts instead of dumping arbitrary records.
- Context reserves only connector origin and correlation metadata; caller-supplied reserved `usl_*` values are removed.
- Domains are typed: a leaf is `[field path, operator, value]` with an enumerated operator, and `&`/`|`/`!` arity is checked the way Odoo's own `normalize_domain` checks it. A malformed filter is rejected before any Odoo call.
- Relational (x2many) values accept raw Odoo command tuples or the named form `{link|unlink|delete|set: [ids]}`, `{create: [values]}`, `{update: [{id, values}]}`, `{clear: true}`, lowered to those tuples in a fixed order.
- `company_ids`, `lang`, and `active_test` are named parameters that map onto `allowed_company_ids`, `lang`, and `active_test`. They override the same key supplied inside `context` and report the override as a warning.
- `odoo_describe_model` projects and caps its payload. It returns `fields_page`/`methods_page` totals; absence must be read from those, not from the returned keys.
- `odoo_search_records` and `odoo_read_records` accept `fields` for flat reads (many2one values are `[id, display_name]` pairs) or `specification` to read related fields in the same call. A bare `{}` on a relation returns its IDs. With `{"line_ids": {"fields": {"name": {}}, "limit": 1}}`, an order with two lines can return `[{"id": 11, "name": "Service"}, {"id": 12}]`. Odoo takes the first N related IDs from each parent and expands every occurrence of those IDs in the batch. If two contacts share a tag, it can be expanded for both, even when it appears after the limit on one contact.
- To page the actual related rows, search their model with a top-level `limit`. For order lines, filter on the inverse `order_id`. If a relation has no inverse field, get its IDs from the parent and filter the related search with `["id", "in", ids]`. The legacy `odoo_expand_record` tool remains available on the `all` profile.
- `odoo_create_records` and `odoo_update_records` accept the same `specification` and return the records as `read_back`, so no follow-up read is needed. A single create and every update run `web_save`, where the write and the read-back share one Odoo transaction; a batch create runs `create` and then reads the new records back by id through `web_search_read`, because Odoo's `web_save_multi` only writes to records that already exist.
- Searches ordered by `id asc` or `id desc` alone page by keyset: the next page restricts the domain by the last id seen and cannot skip or repeat rows when records are inserted or deleted between pages. Any other order pages by offset. Cursors are bound to the query and carry their mode.
- Every write path that takes a rich-text body states the escaping contract in its own field descriptions. With `description_is_html`, `body_is_html`, or `note_is_html` false, the server escapes the text and turns newlines into `<br>`. With the flag true, the server stores the string as raw HTML and the caller must not escape it. `odoo_update_records` stays the pass-through reference: `values.description` is written exactly as given.
- For `odoo_post_message`, omitting `body_is_html` automatically recognizes HTML formatting (including escaped markup) and sends it as HTML in the same single mutation; ordinary prose stays escaped. An explicit false always keeps tags literal. Task descriptions and activity notes still require the flag for markup. On those task and activity paths, a body carrying recognised HTML tags with no explicit flag is refused in preflight as `markup_declaration_required`, before any Odoo call. This prevents silently storing formatted task descriptions or activity notes as literal tags. An explicit `false` is still honoured, so prose that merely looks tag-shaped stays postable.
- Markdown is rendered in neither mode, and plain text sent with the flag true loses its line breaks. Both return a `warnings` entry rather than a refusal.
- A body that carries the flag true, holds no HTML tag, and holds escaped tags such as `&lt;p&gt;` is decoded before the write, and the decode is reported in `warnings`. Without that guard the record stores visible markup and the call still succeeds.
- `odoo_call_method` reports `execution.mode`. Odoo's published `api` classification selects the contract: `read` for a method Odoo states is readonly, `mutation` otherwise, including when the classification is unknown.


## Original evidence handoff

`documents_attach_source_evidence` uploads a host-supplied file reference or
copies an existing attachment/archived original to an expense or accounting
entry. Provide exactly one `file`, `source_attachment_id` or `source_document_id`.
The original remains unchanged; the destination receives native owned evidence
and optional main selection. See [source evidence handoff](https://github.com/unstaticlabs/odoo-mcp/blob/9f5c5afa6785b2244bf16a50909d13040ef72d3b/docs/source-evidence-handoff.md)
for file inputs, exact-byte/checksum guarantees, native workflow boundaries,
provenance, duplicates and ambiguous-outcome recovery.
